title: The 25 Best Defensive Midfielders in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 18, 2025Rodri has forged quite the legacy. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesIn today’s fast-paced game, defensive midfielders are often the unsung heroes—the relentless engine powering every great team.

They’re not just ball-winners; they’re tacticians, distributors and masters of the tempo. From breaking up attacks to launching precise passes, these players control the game’s rhythm while covering every blade of grass with stamina and smarts.

The role demands total commitment for the full 90 minutes, blending grit with grace and aggression with intelligence—and often, a top-class No. 6 is the difference between victory and defeat, progression or elimination or lifting a trophy instead of settling for second best.

Some players have evolved from classy defensive midfielders into world-beating central midfielders, but there’s still an abundance of quality remaining from those who sit a little deeper. Here, Sports Illustrated ranks the current best in the business.

Andrey Santos traded Chelsea for Man Utd. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesJack of all trades, master of none. Usually a withering insult, it’s actually a complimentary assessment of Andrey Santos and his value in the middle of the field. The Brazilian will never be the glitziest name on any team sheet, but he’s super consistent and boasts the ability to plug many roles within the engine room. Chelsea saw glimpses of his precocious talent during his stint in west London, but Manchester United supporters will be eager to see more frequent servings of his ability. He’s still young, with plenty of time to hone his craft.

Nico González has enormous potential. / Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesNico González was drafted in as Manchester City’s Rodri replacement midway through the 2024–25 season due to an injury to the Ballon d’Or winner. Those are not easy shoes to fill and the Spaniard initially struggled to replicate the lofty standards of his compatriot. However, the enforcer has bucked up his ideas since, and while he’s still operating far below the level of his World Cup-winning compatriot, he’s beginning to find a more consistent level.  González was deemed surplus to requirements as Enzo Maresca ushered in a new era at the Etihad Stadium, resulting in a move to Newcastle United for more regular minutes. Luckily, time is on the midfielder’s side, and he could become a hero on Tyneside.

Ayyoub Bouaddi captured the imagination at the 2026 World Cup. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesMan City set about rebuilding their midfield ahead of Maresca’s first campaign, splashing an absolute fortune on three leading talents: Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi. The latter is the youngest and least experienced of the trio, yet his reputation is sky high after an exceptional 2026 World Cup campaign at the base of Morocco’s midfield. Despite his tender age, Bouaddi delivered a stream of graceful yet combative performances—those more fitting of someone 10 years his senior. Bouaddi’s already a terrific midfielder. He should get even better in the years to come.

James Garner has blossomed on Merseyside. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester United have allowed some talented academy graduates to slip through their fingers over the past decade, and James Garner is yet another example of their negligence. Ironically, many of the club’s recent difficulties in midfield could have been solved by the Englishman, whose no-nonsense performances for Everton have earned him widespread acclaim. Garner is a formidable presence in the No.6 position with his endless energy reserves and crunching challenges, but he’s also a classy distributor with terrific vision. It’s no surprise he’s now a senior England international.

N’Golo Kanté continues to deliver year on year. / Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu/Getty ImagesHe might be deep into the twilight of his career and playing his soccer in Türkiye, but trust us when we say—N’Golo Kanté has still absolutely got it.Kante may be racking up the miles, but the engine’s still running at full throttle. The French midfielder covers every single blade of grass, motoring around the center of the field extinguishing fires and reclaiming possession. The World Cup and two-time Premier League winner might be playing outside of Europe’s elite divisions, but Fenerbahçe supporters can attest to his consistently excellent performances. Everybody seemingly has a soft spot for Kanté.

Morten Hjulmand is ever so consistent. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAfter honing his craft at Admira Wacker and then Lecce, Morten Hjulmand earned his big break with a move to Portuguese giants Sporting CP in the summer of 2023.The Dane quietly became one of the most important pieces in Sporting’s setup, playing a central role in historic back-to-back Liga Portugal titles. While goal-machine Viktor Gyökeres grabbed the headlines each week, Hjulmand was one of the squad’s unsung heroes.A defensively intelligent midfielder with an excellent read of the game, Hjulmand anticipates danger before it fully develops. Time and again, he’s the one to break up opposition attacks, turning defense into swift counter attacks that often end with a ball in behind.Hjulmand has taken his talents to Atlético Madrid, where Diego Simeone is certain to put them to effective use.

Carlos Baleba finally earned his Old Trafford move. / Dan Mullan/Getty ImagesDefensive midfielders are usually known for being strong, powerful and—if we’re being honest—a bit rigid. Carlos Baleba is anything but that. He combines sheer athleticism with the traditional traits of a holding midfielder, making him one of the most unique talents around.Baleba brings defensive resilience in spades—breaking up play with real bite, blocking everything in sight—but pairs it with exceptional ball-carrying ability. A true carry-first type of player, his first instinct upon winning the ball is to surge into open space, which has proven to be a nightmare for opposing teams.Once he’s upfield, he’ll either pick a pass or unleash a long-range strike—something that Man Utd supporters will have the pleasure of witnessing over the coming seasons.

Eduardo Camavinga is incredibly versatile. / Mateo Villalba/Getty ImagesA string of untimely injuries—plus Carlo Ancelotti’s decision to regularly deploy him at left-back—has somewhat dented the reputation of Eduardo Camavinga.But in our eyes? He’s still the same all-action, graceful-yet-gritty defensive midfielder who took the world by storm as a teenager at the 2022 World Cup and played a crucial role in Real Madrid’s La Liga and Champions League doubles in both 2021–22 and 2023–24.His Madrid teammates now affectionately call him “Lizarazu,” in reference to the legendary French left-back—but we prefer the nickname “Tacklevinga,” one he earned as a youngster in France. And for good reason. With those long telescopic legs, elite reading of the game, serious recovery pace and strength in duels, there are few players tougher to get past in the middle of the pitch.

Rúben Neves is still going strong in Saudi Arabia. / Abdullah Ahmed/Getty ImagesIn 2017, Rúben Neves opted to leave Portuguese giants FC Porto in order to join Wolverhampton Wanderers, then of the Championship. It was a deal that baffled many, with observers wondering why a player so talented would drop into the second tier of English football.But Neves knew what he was buying into at Wolves. Alongside Ivan Cavaleiro and Diogo Jota, he helped fire the Old Gold into the Premier League at the first time of asking, flourishing under the management of Nuno Espírito Santo. Fast forward another 12 months and Wolves had cemented a top seven finish—a remarkable achievement that owed much to the individual brilliance of Neves.Neves offered technical guile, composure and a range of passing that Wolves supporters had never seen before. He oozed class, demonstrated tremendous leadership and pulled the level up of those around him.Now in Saudi Arabia with Al Hilal, Neves doesn’t get to test his skills against Europe’s finest week in, week out, but demonstrates how good he remains every time he represents Portugal in international competition.

Adam Wharton has plenty of admirers. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesAdam Wharton doesn’t have the flashiest name—and he’s certainly not the flashiest player. But make no mistake: the Crystal Palace midfielder is the real deal.Calm, composed and endlessly reliable, Wharton has built a reputation for outplaying some of the biggest names in the game—without ever breaking a sweat. Just ask Kevin De Bruyne and Bernardo Silva, who were both stifled by the 20-year-old in the 2025 FA Cup final, as Palace shocked Man City to lift the trophy.Tracking every run, breaking up every attack and distributing with the kind of precision that would make De Bruyne proud—Wharton controls the midfield with smart, effective passing.There’s a reason he has such an extensive list of admirers.

An incredible free signing for Aston Villa. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesAston Villa’s progress under Unai Emery was often attribute to those who stole the headlines before their departures—Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans. But in the background was the glue holding everything together; Boubacar Kamara.The Frenchman provides the stable platform for others to shine from, doing all of the dirty work in midfield while mopping things up when possession is lost. He does the simple things, ticking the ball over to get Villa further up the field.Kamara is also more than capable of playing a defense-splitting pass of his own—he often advances the ball forward to help Villa transition from defense to attack. Breaking at speed is one of Villa’s most eye-catching traits and it’s made possible by Kamara’s ability to steal the ball back and switch from reverse gear into full throttle.

An ever-present in Inter Milan’s midfield. / Denis Doyle/Getty ImagesHakan Çalhanoğlu isn’t your typical defensive midfielder.Originally deployed as a more advanced playmaker, the Turkish international has gradually dropped deeper into midfield in recent years—yet he’s lost none of the attacking flair that made him such a standout in the first place.Now orchestrating play from deep for Inter Milan, Çalhanoğlu brings a rare blend of defensive intelligence and offensive firepower. He reads the game brilliantly, dictates tempo with poise and—crucially—still carries a serious threat from range.Give him space, even 30 yards from goal, and you’re asking for trouble. With a cannon of a right foot, he’s capable of rifling in top-corner screamers at will.

One of the game’s brightest talents. / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty Images.In a Bayern Munich squad stacked with star power, it was the quietly composed Aleksandar Pavlović who emerged as one of the real surprises of 2024–25.The midfielder had already earned his first senior Germany call-up in March 2024—a sign that those behind the scenes were paying attention. But it was in the months that followed where he truly began to shine on a bigger stage. Stepping into Bayern’s midfield with minimal fuss, he brought calm, control and maturity well beyond his years.Pavlović further blossomed during a successful 2025–26 season, regularly showcasing his sharp positional sense, composed distribution and intelligent decision-making—traits which earned him a place in Germany’s most recent World Cup roster. He’s not flashy, but he’s incredibly effective. And while he may have flown under the radar at first, Pavlović is now firmly in the spotlight—and looking every bit like a future cornerstone for both club and country.

Angelo Stiller continues to go underappreciated. / Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesIf Joshua Kimmich is the heir apparent to Philipp Lahm, then Angelo Stiller might just be next big star following in Kimmich’s own footsteps.A product of the Bayern academy—where he undoubtedly studied Kimmich’s game—Stiller now shines at Stuttgart and looks every bit the natural successor for Germany’s midfield maestro. Like Kimmich, he blends razor-sharp ball control with relentless defensive tenacity, and he’s a tactical chameleon—equally adept at pulling the strings in midfield, stepping into central defense or bursting forward as a winger when called upon.The likeness is striking. While he’s still carving his path to Kimmich’s elite level, all signs point to Stiller becoming a major force for club and country.

Granit Xhaka has aged like a fine wine. / George Wood/Getty ImagesGranit Xhaka was once the Premier League’s favorite scapegoat. Known more for his red cards than his passing range, the Swiss midfielder’s time at Arsenal reached a low point in October 2019, when he was jeered off the pitch by his own fans—a moment that seemed like the end.But Mikel Arteta’s arrival gave Xhaka a second chance and he slowly rebuilt his reputation in north London. That said, few would have predicted the full-blown renaissance that awaited him in Germany.At Bayer Leverkusen, Xhaka underwent a total transformation—from hot-headed liability to elite midfield general. As the heartbeat of Xabi Alonso’s undefeated Bundesliga-winning side in 2023–24, he thrived in a deeper, more orchestrated role.Now, he's the one pulling the strings at Sunderland—dictating tempo, threading line-breaking passes and acting as the anchor for the overperforming Black Cats.
